note: Laid out to follow the in-game settings menu: the same sections, in the same order, with settings grouped the way CS2 groups them. It is a close mapping rather than a pixel copy -- the authority on the menu is the game, and this is assembled from what can actually be read and written on disk.

sources.cfg: a convar in a .cfg / .vcfg file; editable by this tool
sources.video: a key in cs2_video.txt under Steam userdata; CS2 ignores these as console convars, so they can only be set in that file

control_note: A slider appears only where the engine clamps the value to a known range. Anything unbounded gets a number box, because a slider implies limits and inventing them would misrepresent what the game accepts. 'range_source' says which is which.

setting.defaultres.label: Resolution width
setting.defaultres.help: Set this in the game's own video menu; changing it here can leave you unable to see the game.

setting.aspectratiomode.label: Aspect ratio mode
setting.aspectratiomode.help: Meaning of each value is not documented outside the game; left read-only rather than guessed at.

setting.fullscreen_min_on_focus_loss.label: Minimise on focus loss
setting.fullscreen_min_on_focus_loss.help: Off keeps the game up when you alt-tab, which is most of the alt-tab pause.

setting.mat_vsync.label: Wait for vertical sync
setting.mat_vsync.help: Adds about a frame of latency and caps you at the refresh rate.

snd_mute_losefocus.label: Audio when game is in background

snd_mute_mvp_music_live_players.label: Mute MVP music with live players

engine_no_focus_sleep.label: Sleep when unfocused
engine_no_focus_sleep.help: 0 keeps the frame rate up when the window loses focus.

sensitivity.label: Mouse sensitivity
sensitivity.help: No slider: the engine accepts a very wide range and any bound here would be invented.

fps_max.label: Frame rate cap
fps_max.help: 0 is unlimited. No slider: there is no meaningful upper bound to draw one against.

rate.label: Max bandwidth
rate.help: CS2 defaults to 786432, which is also the maximum. Older configs often carry a CS:GO-era 128000.

cl_mute_all_but_friends_and_party.label: Mute all but friends and party

snd_mixahead.label: Audio buffer ahead
snd_mixahead.help: Lower reduces audio latency but risks crackling. Not exposed in the game's menu.

cl_predict_kill_ragdolls.label: Predict kill ragdolls
cl_predict_kill_ragdolls.help: Damage prediction plays the hit feedback immediately instead of waiting for the server to confirm it. It feels more responsive, and it can be wrong -- aim punch, tagging, or a death your client has not seen yet can produce feedback for a hit that did not land. This one is on by default; the other two are off.

cl_predict_body_shot_fx.label: Predict body shot effects
cl_predict_body_shot_fx.help: Damage prediction plays the hit feedback immediately instead of waiting for the server to confirm it. It feels more responsive, and it can be wrong -- aim punch, tagging, or a death your client has not seen yet can produce feedback for a hit that did not land.

cl_predict_head_shot_fx.label: Predict head shot effects
cl_predict_head_shot_fx.help: Damage prediction plays the hit feedback immediately instead of waiting for the server to confirm it. It feels more responsive, and it can be wrong -- aim punch, tagging, or a death your client has not seen yet can produce feedback for a hit that did not land.

cl_disable_ragdolls.label: Disable ragdolls
cl_disable_ragdolls.help: Removes corpse physics entirely. Saves CPU and clears the view, but you lose the body as a marker of where someone died.

cl_ragdoll_limit.label: Maximum ragdolls
cl_ragdoll_limit.help: How many corpses stay on screen. -1 is no limit.

layout_note: Three levels: section, category, sub-category. A setting with no explicit sub-category falls back to the first one in its category, so nothing is ever hidden by being unclassified.
